age.evidence: All mice were housed in groups of 5 and weighed between 35 and 55 g and were 3 -4 months in age.

sex.evidence: Male Swiss-Webster mice (CFW: Charles River Laboratories, INC Wilmington, MA) served as the subjects in all experiments.

dosing.evidence: an injection of either R( -)DOI (0.1, 0.32, 1.0, 3.2, or 10 mg/kg) was administered and subsequent HTR was recorded; All compounds were dissolved in sterile saline and delivered through intraperitoneal injection
This same acute pretreatment protocol was used to evaluate the effects of fluoxetine on psilocybin-induced HTR (0.32, 1, 1.8, 3.2, and 10 mg/kg).

dosing.doses_raw: fluoxetine (10 or 32 mg/kg); daily injections of either saline or 10 mg/kg fluoxetine
dosing.evidence: acute refers to a single administration of fluoxetine 30 min prior to psychedelic administration, while chronic refers to daily fluoxetine administration over 14 days with the final administration occurring 30 min before psychedelic administration.

handling.evidence: Only mention: 'animals were handled repeatedly during testing sessions' — not a pre-test handling habituation protocol.

group_housing.evidence: All mice were housed in groups of 5

day_night_flipped.evidence: The lights were turned off at 7 p.m. and turned back on at 7 a.m. every day. All experiments were conducted during the light phase.

assays.assay_description: Mice injected i.p. with R(-)DOI or psilocybin and placed individually in acrylic chambers; video recorded for 10 min beginning 10 min post-injection and HTR counted offline by two trained observers. Dose-response functions under acute fluoxetine (10 or 32 mg/kg), chronic fluoxetine (10 mg/kg x14 d), and 14-day discontinuation pretreatment conditions (psilocybin only with acute fluoxetine).

application_type.evidence: All compounds were dissolved in sterile saline and delivered through intraperitoneal injection

setup_habituation.evidence: Only room acclimation described: 'male Swiss-Webster mice were set in a room to acclimate for 30 min.'

setup_restrain.evidence: were placed individually into acrylic chambers, where a video recording system was set up above for subsequent offline scoring

food_restriction.evidence: Test conducted in acrylic chambers separate from home cage; food ad libitum only in home cage ('Mice had access to food ... and water ad libitum').

water_restriction.evidence: Test conducted in acrylic chambers separate from home cage; no water in testing chamber described.

time_to_assay.evidence: HTR behavior in each subject was recorded 10 min postinjection of each psychedelic and recorded for a duration of 10 min.

sample_size.evidence: N = 5 -14 (Figure 1, 2 captions); Tables 1-2 list group Ns from 5 to 14

outcomes.summary: DOI and psilocybin produced dose-dependent (inverted-U) increases in HTR. Acute 32 mg/kg (but not 10 mg/kg) fluoxetine reduced DOI potency (~10-fold ED50 shift); chronic 10 mg/kg fluoxetine reduced DOI efficacy (Emax) without changing potency, an effect that recovered after 14-day discontinuation. Acute 10 mg/kg fluoxetine reduced psilocybin Emax without altering potency.
outcomes.evidence: Thus, chronic fluoxetine decreases the efficacy but not the potency of DOI-induced HTR. ... Thus, acute fluoxetine attenuates the maximal behavioral response to psilocybin without altering its potency.

B1_num_measures.evidence: HTR counts (Mean ± SEM); ED50/Emax are curve parameters derived from the single HTR count measure.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: HTR reported as total counts over the 10-min recording; no within-session time course.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioural transitions or sequences reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is excluded by rubric; paper describes it as 'distinguishable from species typical grooming and scratching behaviors'.

B6_cognitive.evidence: HTR is a drug-elicited unlearned response.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Each session was scored by two trained observers

B8_multivariate.evidence: Nonlinear regression of dose-response curves with extra-sum-of-squares F tests; no multivariate behavioural analysis.

E2_shelter.evidence: No shelter described in the acrylic chambers.

E3_bedding.evidence: No bedding described in the acrylic chambers.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water described inside the testing chambers.

D1_continuity.evidence: For chronic and discontinuation doses, mice were tested twice (once at the end of chronic dosing and again at the end of the discontinuation phase).

D2_session_duration.evidence: recorded for a duration of 10 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: mice were tested twice (once at the end of chronic dosing and again at the end of the discontinuation phase)

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline HTR recording reported.

D5_followup.evidence: Every HTR session, including the discontinuation test, was recorded 10 min after a fresh psychedelic injection ('HTR behavior in each subject was recorded 10 min postinjection of each psychedelic'); no recording >=24 h after last drug administration.

D6_circadian.evidence: recorded for a duration of 10 min

judge_notes: All candidates agreed on a single HTR assay; acute, chronic, discontinuation and DOI/psilocybin arms collapsed into one assay per rubric.
B1 set to 0 (1 measure): ED50/Emax are derived parameters of the single HTR count, not distinct behavioural measures (overrode deepseek4; gemma4's score of 1 conflicted with its own value '1').

D5 set to 0 against two candidates: the discontinuation-phase recording occurred 10 min after a new DOI injection, so no recording was >=24 h after the last drug administration; the 14-day gap applies only to fluoxetine.
setup_habituation set to not_reported: only 30-min room acclimation described, which the rubric excludes.
handling set to not_reported: 'handled repeatedly during testing sessions' is not a pre-test handling protocol.

Outcome direction set to 'increase' (psychedelics increased HTR); fluoxetine attenuation described in summary. time_dependent set to n/a because time from psychedelic to test was a single 10-min timepoint.
Fluoxetine added to dosing as a co-administered drug (acute 10/32 mg/kg and chronic 10 mg/kg x14 d); qPCR was excluded as non-behavioural.
n_total left null: group Ns are listed in the tables, but animal reuse across chronic and discontinuation tests and ambiguous table labels make an exact total uncertain.
